question: When are no-passing-zone markings required at horizontal or vertical curves, and what should be done when successive no-passing zones are separated by less than 400 feet?
model_answer: # Answer Direct Answer: On roadways with center line markings, no-passing-zone markings are mandatory at horizontal or vertical curves wherever the passing sight distance falls below the minimum in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit (e.g., 450 feet at 25 mph up to 1,200 feet at 70 mph). When successive no-passing zones are separated by less than 400 feet, the no-passing zone markings should be connected to join the zones. Standards (mandatory): - "On roadways with center line markings, no-passing zone markings shall be used at horizontal or vertical curves where the passing sight distance is less than the minimum shown in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit." - "On two-way, two-lane or three-lane roadways where center line markings are installed, no-passing zones shall be established at vertical and horizontal curves and other locations where an engineering study indicates that passing must be prohibited because of inadequate sight distances or other special conditions." - "No-passing zones shall be marked by either the one-direction no-passing zone pavement markings or the two-direction no-passing zone pavement markings described in Section 3B.01 and shown in Figures 3B-1 and 3B-3." - "No-passing zone markings shall be used on: A. Two-way roadways at lane-reduction transitions (see Section 3B.12), B. Approaches to obstructions that must be passed on the right (see Section 3B.13), C. Approaches to grade crossings (see Section 8C.02), and D. Approaches to crosswalks." Guidance (recommended): - "Where the distance between successive no-passing zones is less than 400 feet, no-passing zone markings should connect the zones." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3B-4 illustrates the method of locating no-passing zone limits at vertical and horizontal curves, with the zone beginning at point "a" where sight distance (measured between points 3.5 feet above the pavement) first becomes less than the minimum and ending at point "b" where sight distance again exceeds the minimum. - [Image 2] Table 3B-1 lists the minimum passing sight distances that trigger no-passing zone markings, ranging from 450 feet at 25 mph to 1,200 feet at 70 mph. - [Image 3] Page 584 shows the same table and explains that the upstream end of a no-passing zone (point "a") is where sight distance first drops below the Table 3B-1 value and the downstream end (point "b") is where it again exceeds the minimum, along with the 400-foot connection guidance. - [Image 4] Page 585 (Figure 3B-4) shows profile and plan views of no-passing zones at vertical and horizontal curves, noting that zones in opposite directions might or might not overlap depending on alignment. - [Image 5] Page 583 contains Section 3B.03 with the Standard provisions listing where no-passing zone markings shall be used, including at curves where an engineering study indicates passing must be prohibited due to inadequate sight distances. - [Image 6] Page 1051 (Figure 8C-1) shows an example of no-passing zone application on an approach to a grade crossing, including the optional W14-3 NO PASSING ZONE sign. Citations: - Section 3B.03 Standard §4 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §3 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §2 (p.542) - Section 3B.03 Standard §1 (p.542) - Section 3B.03 Guidance §7 (p.543) - Section 2B.36 Support §3 (p.102) - Figure 3B-4 (p.544) - Table 3B-1 (p.543) - Page 584 - Page 585 - Page 583 - Page 1051
gold_answer: They are required on roadways with center line markings where passing sight distance is below the minimum in Table 3B-1 for the relevant speed. If successive no-passing zones are less than 400 feet apart, the markings should connect the zones.
